subject: Re: Quantization rollout caused throughput collapse and partial decode failures
messages:
From: Aisha Mehta <aisha.mehta@lodestar.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Carlos Vega <c.vega@lodestar.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T07:05:00-08:00
Subject: Sudden throughput drop + 2% completion error after this morning's qprofile push

Hannah / Carlos,

We deployed Redwood's qprofile-v4-int8 to our canary pool at 03:40 UTC and immediately saw overall throughput drop ~45% for our short-sequence payment tokenization requests. Simultaneously completion error callbacks climbed to ~2% (from ~0.02%). This is impacting our reconciliation job and a low-latency webhook consumer.

We did not change client-side batching. Attached are a handful of traces and client logs for the window. Can you confirm whether any kernel selection changes, new fused kernels, or batching heuristic adjustments were released with that qprofile? We need a mitigation path within the day because our production ramp is scheduled Wednesday.

Thanks,
Aisha Mehta
SRE Lead, Lodestar AI

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Mehta <aisha.mehta@lodestar.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T07:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 2% completion error after this morning's qprofile push

Hi Aisha 6 Carlos 6 thanks for the quick alert and artifacts. I'm escalating to runtime and SRE now.

Initial notes: our nightly optimizer did promote a qprofile tuning candidate (qprofile-v4-int8) around 03:15 UTC that carries a new kernel affinity rule intended to prefer a fused GEMM path on our A100p and H100 pools. We'll validate whether that affinity flipped for your canary hosts.

Immediate actions from Redwood:
- Markus (runtime) to validate kernel affinity and replicate under Lodestar's short-sequence histogram.
- Marissa (SRE) to prepare a routing override to pin your canary and staging routes to the previous qprofile (v4-fp16) and to perform a rolling rollback if needed.
- Irene to collect host-level metrics (nvprof, dispatch timing) and correlate with request-size buckets.

I will follow up with a mitigation ETA within 30 minutes.

 Hannah
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T07:40:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Sudden throughput drop + 2% completion error after this morning's qprofile push

Quick findings: reproducer in our lab with Lodestar's trace shows that the fused GEMM kernel has a higher per-dispatch overhead for short sequences (<48 tokens) and interacts poorly with our continuous-batching window. The net effect: fewer tokens per second and increased decode fallbacks when the int8 path hits an alignment case in the decoder (we see an exception path that triggers a software decode fallback).

Mitigation plan:
1) Push routing override to pin Lodestar canaries to v4-fp16 (done as config draft).
2) Roll back the kernel-affinity rule for qprofile-v4-int8 on canary hosts (rolling) 6 should see throughput recover within 5-12 minutes per host.
3) Add an immediate runtime safety: disable fused GEMM preference for short-sequence workloads until the fused kernel is validated end-to-end.

I am applying the rollback to a subset of canaries now and will stream metrics.

 Markus
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-02T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 2% completion error after this morning's qprofile push

Hi Aisha 6 update and observed numbers from the first rollback tranche.

Actions taken:
- Rolled back kernel-affinity and pinned canaries to v4-fp16 at 07:58 UTC (rolling).
- Temporary routing override applied for your canary and staging routes.

Observed impact:
- Throughput on pinned canaries recovered to ~94% of previous baseline within ~9 minutes of host restart/transition.
- Completion error rate fell from 2.0% to 0.15% on the pinned hosts but a few noisy hosts still show intermittent decode fallback traces.

Next steps:
- Markus will run a targeted microbenchmark on fused GEMM with Lodestar's token histogram and we will ship a patch to the kernel-selection heuristic to avoid preferring the fused path for short sequences.
- We'll request approval for a controlled production rollback window if staging remains stable.

 Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Mehta <aisha.mehta@lodestar.ai>, Carlos Vega <c.vega@lodestar.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-03-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Status and ask: candidate rollback window for Lodestar production

Hi Aisha / Carlos 6 morning status after overnight validation.

Summary:
- Canary and staging are stable with routing pinned to v4-fp16; throughput and error rates returned to expected baselines.
- Root cause: fused GEMM kernel preferred by qprofile-v4-int8 has higher dispatch overhead for short sequences, and an alignment edge-case triggers a decoder fallback in ~0.1% of requests which surfaced as 2% under your workload due to batching interactions.
- We have a reproducible unit test and a patch ready that adjusts kernel-selection heuristics and adds a metric to detect the dispatch-overhead skew early.

Proposal:
- Targeted production rollback to v4-fp16 for Lodestar on 2027-03-04 01:00-03:00 UTC (rolling) with on-call coordination and post-rollback smoke tests. This will be a conservative rollback to avoid your ramp-day risk.

Ask: please confirm the window or propose an alternative. We'll provide the rollback runbook and reserve rollback capacity to avoid transient throttling during the switch.

Thanks for the rapid collaboration 6 your traces made this diagnosable very quickly.

 Hannah
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
